D2EinfachauswahlGrundlagenSkill 2.1.6

Eine Python-App soll im selben Projekt einen Foundry-Agent anlegen und Cloud-Evaluierungen ausführen. Welchen Client sollte die App zuerst erzeugen?

AzureOpenAI fixiert nur eine API-Version für Modellaufrufe; Projekt-Features fehlen, und statt schlüsselloser Anmeldung wird ein Key genutzt.

Der Projekt-Client legt Agents an und konfiguriert das Projekt; sein get_openai_client() liefert den OpenAI-kompatiblen Client, der Responses, Agents und Evaluierungen ausführt.

ARM ist die Control Plane zum Anlegen und Konfigurieren von Ressourcen, nicht die Data Plane für Agents und Evaluierungsläufe.

narrative.overview:
AI-103 Prep is a Microsoft Learn–style study app assembled from Fluent 2 parts: a #f5f5f5 ground, white panels lifted by soft two-part shadows, one brand blue, the Segoe UI stack for everything you read and Cascadia Code for everything you type. It does not reinvent the category; it plays it straight and puts the craft where the direction contract puts it, “in the guided path and the step-through diagrams,” and where PRODUCT.md puts it, in “the precision of every state.”

The density is a study desk's: data-dense where the learner checks where they stand (31 stations, readiness meters, the skills map, tables) and generous where they read (prose held near 54 characters at 15–17px). Picture first: every lesson opens on a hand-built SVG diagram whose nodes are typed by tone and whose steps light one part at a time while the rest recedes but stays legible. Every screen keeps the next step in view: the “Als Nächstes dran” card, the Wiederholen count in the nav, the session bar's single “Weiter”.

Two rejections are confirmed. The generic card-grid dashboard template: the contract's thesis refuses it, so the home is a guided path beside a next-step column, not a grid of stat tiles. And gamification: no achievement badges, streak pressure or confetti. The craft bar is Microsoft Learn, Khan Academy and Duolingo without the game layer.
keyCharacteristics: Fluent 2 neutrals: a #f5f5f5 ground with white panels at 8px corners on the soft shadow-4.
One brand blue (#0f6cbd) for “act here” and “you are here”; status green and red appear only after an answer is revealed.
Five domain hues for the five exam domains and nine diagram tones for node types, always paired with words.
Segoe UI stack, sentence case, no uppercase, tabular numerals for every count.
Signatures: the step-through diagram (typed tones, six shapes, measured labels, focus/context/dim) and the guided path of stations.
Phones get a five-tab bar plus a Menü; sticky parts stick only while they fit.

rules.name: The You-Are-Here Rule
rules.body: Brand blue means “act here” or “you are here”: a primary button, the current step, the next station, the lit arrow, the focus ring. It never decorates.

rules.name: The Domain Hue Rule
rules.body: The five domain hues identify exam domains and nothing else. Domain-coloured text uses its -ink step on its -tint; icons, bars and dots use the fill.

rules.name: The Verdict Rule
rules.body: Green and red appear only after an answer is revealed, and always with an icon and a word (check or dismiss circle plus “richtig” or “falsch”, “Nicht ganz”), never colour alone.

rules.name: The Typed Tone Rule
rules.body: In diagrams colour encodes node type, never order or emphasis. Emphasis belongs to the step state, and every diagram carries a legend of the tones it uses.

rules.name: The Reading Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose holds near 54ch: the lesson lead, callouts, traps and takeaways, the question stem, the explanation. Diagram narration and caption run to 56ch, per-option explanations to 56ch plus their 64px indent. Explanatory text never runs the full panel width.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Nothing is uppercased: titles, buttons, tabs and labels are sentence-case German. The only positive tracking in the system is the domain chip's +0.02em.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every number that counts or changes (badges, chips, step dots, percentages, timers, scores, skill IDs, dates) uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Sticky-Only-If-It-Fits Rule
rules.body: A column sticks only while all of it fits the window; nothing may end up out of reach. Case-study panels cap their height and scroll inside.

rules.name: The Next-Step-First Rule
rules.body: When columns collapse, “Als Nächstes dran” moves to the top.

rules.name: The No-Sideways-Page Rule
rules.body: The page itself never scrolls sideways, down to 320px. Only diagram canvases, code blocks and, above 560px, wide tables scroll inside their own frame; grid tracks that hold questions, results or code are `minmax(0, 1fr)` so a long line can't widen them.

rules.name: The Finger-Size Rule
rules.body: Where the main pointer is a finger, targets are at least 44px tall: buttons, segmented controls, selects, list and table links, breadcrumbs. Icon buttons, diagram step dots, filter chips and skills tiles are at least 40px, and each whole guided-path station is one tap target. Selects use 16px text so iOS never zooms the page on focus.

rules.name: The Soft Fluent Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth uses only the shipped Fluent ramp: never a hard offset shadow, never a heavier custom one.

rules.name: The Flat-Inside Rule
rules.body: Inside a panel, containers rest flat; shadow appears there only in response to the learner (the hovered thumbnail, the focused diagram node).

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: 8px contains, 4px controls; anything rounder is a position marker, a status pill or a diagram form.

rules.name: The Next-Step Signal Rule
rules.body: The Wiederholen count stays in the navigation on purpose: it is Product Principle 1 (“Always show the next step”) in the chrome, a pointer to due work rather than a reward.

rules.name: The Readable Recede Rule
rules.body: When a step lights its parts, the rest recedes but stays legible: fills and strokes fade, text only turns Receded Text Grey (at least 3:1), and the endpoints of a lit arrow stay at full strength as context.

rules.name: The Twenty-Pixel Rule
rules.body: An edge label sits on its arrow only when at least 20px of arrow stays visible on each side; otherwise it moves beside the arrow (above or right first, then below or left), clear of nodes, group titles, other labels and other arrows.

rules.name: The Real-Edge Rule
rules.body: The thumbnail draws an arrow only where the diagram has an edge between those two nodes; everywhere else it leaves a plain gap.

dos: Do put content on white panels (8px, shadow-4) on the #f5f5f5 ground, 20px apart.
Do keep brand blue for the next action and the current position, and use -ink text on -tint fills for every tinted label.
Do pair every verdict colour with an icon and a word, and show it only after the answer is revealed.

Do build every concept diagram from the nine typed tones and six shapes, with a legend, numbered steps, narration and the focus, context and dim states, and ship it only at 0 validator and render-audit errors in EN and DE.
Do hold prose near 54ch (56ch for diagram narration and captions).
Do draw icons from the generated Fluent set (20px viewBox, currentColor).
Do keep the Wiederholen due count in the navigation (a dot on phones): it shows the next step.
Do make sticky columns conditional on fitting the window, and let “Als Nächstes dran” lead when columns collapse.
Do keep every question type keyboard-operable: radios behind the letters, up/down buttons for ordering, selects for matching.
Do honour reduced motion: the build collapses every transition and animation, the flowing arrow and smooth scrolling included.
donts: Don't build the generic card-grid dashboard template; the home is a guided path beside a next-step column.
Don't add achievement badges, streak pressure or confetti.
Don't use domain hues for status or decoration, or green and red before an answer is revealed.
Don't use hard offset shadows or anything outside the Fluent shadow ramp, and don't shadow containers that rest inside a panel.
Don't uppercase labels or track them out; the domain chip's +0.02em is the only positive tracking.
Don't let colour carry meaning alone in a diagram; tones always come with text labels and a legend.
Don't draw a thumbnail arrow where the diagram has no edge, hyphenate code tokens, or start a line with “·”.
Don't route an arrow through a node or a group title, or sit an edge label on an arrow that would show less than 20px on either side.
Don't dim diagram text below Receded Text Grey (#858585).
Don't use Microsoft logos or imply endorsement; the app's mark is the 103 square, and the footer says it is not an official Microsoft product.
